editorial:
You meet Precious, a 16-year-old in Harlem who hides a secret: she cannot read, even though she has reached ninth grade. At home, her mother treats her like a servant and hurts her with words and fists, while her father has left her pregnant again. School is loud and messy, but a new teacher sees something in her and pushes her toward a better path. The movie feels heavy but honest, with moments of hope breaking through the pain.

The acting is the big draw, especially the lead performance that makes Precious feel real and brave. The story can be hard to watch because of abuse and trauma, so take breaks if needed. Still, it is powerful and worth your time if you like character-driven dramas. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or buy the 4K Blu-ray.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Precious confronts her mother, who admits she knew about the abuse and let it happen. Precious refuses to stay and takes her two children with her. She moves into a halfway house connected to her school program and starts planning a future on her own terms. The ending is not a fairy tale, but it shows her choosing herself and her kids.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves powerful character dramas and strong performances.
